name: Travis County Exposition Center
summary: County event venue in east Austin where UT Austin nursing students supported a community flu-vaccination event on November 7, 2020.
descriptionParagraphs: The Travis County Exposition Center is a county-owned event venue on Decker Lane in east Austin. On November 7, 2020, a UT Austin School of Nursing volunteer notice described nursing students, supervised by faculty, supporting a community flu-vaccination event there.

The notice was written for student volunteers, so it does not describe who could receive a vaccine, what it cost or how to get an appointment. This page records that one documented event; it does not mean the venue offers vaccinations today. For current services, use Austin Public Health's immunization resources.

name: Montopolis Recreation and Community Center
summary: City recreation center in southeast Austin that hosted a free Austin Public Health mpox vaccination clinic on August 24, 2024.
descriptionParagraphs: The Montopolis Recreation and Community Center is a City of Austin facility on Montopolis Drive. On August 24, 2024, Austin Public Health held a free mpox vaccination clinic there with support from the Austin–Travis County Medical Reserve Corps, according to a contemporaneous news report and corroborating city material.

The event report does not establish whether appointments were required. The center's normal operating hours are recreation-center hours, not vaccination hours. This page records the documented clinic; for current vaccination services, use Austin Public Health's immunization resources.

name: Austin First Spanish SDA Church
summary: North Austin church where the UT Austin nursing VAMOS program conducted COVID-19 vaccination outreach documented in 2021.
descriptionParagraphs: Austin First Spanish SDA Church is on West Rundberg Lane in north Austin. A UT Austin School of Nursing report describes the VAMOS program conducting COVID-19 vaccination outreach at the church in 2021 as part of mobile vaccination efforts reaching Austin-area Hispanic communities.

The report does not state a price or a formal appointment process, and it does not establish that the church offers vaccinations today. For current services, use Austin Public Health's immunization resources.
